[EDIT 6/12/24: This is one of those games that has a VERY good concept with pleasing visuals and silly core mechanics. But with all that aside, you gotta have to be mindful of the ACTUAL gameplay. In it's current state, there exists a handful of major bugs and missing features that take away from the over all enjoyability of the game. Enjoyability you would otherwise have if these issues were addressed and tackled. I believe with time and advice taken from the community, the devs could very well have an insanely successful game. But in its current state, I cannot say that I recommend the game just yet. But please!!! Look out for this game! It is very fun, cute, and unserious in the best way possible! Its a gem, but it still needs to be refined.] You can cannibalize, witness murder, do murder, harvest organs, crucify your enemies, and customize your sinners in this tomo-like colony sim. What else is there to like? Has it all honestly. Despite being in early access, and having the expected major bug here and there, it is a delightful and aesthetically pleasing sim!

This is the first game in years that I IMMEDIATELY knew I needed to play. This game's concept is very compelling: a village of sinners surviving the rapture. The devs clearly understand their source material, such as its references to spirituality, religion, My Sims, Animal Crossing, Tomodachi Life, and various things Gen Z would find nostalgic. The dialogue is littered with humor. This game could become huge; however, I cannot recommend this game right now. As much as the bugs are frustrating and occasionally game-breaking, what really caused me to stop playing was how the game felt hard without being rewarding. [hr][/hr] My constructive criticism: There is no system to notify you when your villagers accomplish something, so I had nothing to celebrate or feel good about. For example, if I completed a study, I wouldn't know unless I checked the church and saw an empty slot for the current study. It's missing some moments of subtle emotional fulfillment. On a bigger scale, my decisions felt meaningless. Progress felt too slow to keep my village alive, even in classic mode. If I focused on making food, my villagers wouldn't make enough and eventually die. The game isn't very balanced right now. It would take an entire day to make one piece of bread or two pieces of barley while my village completed religious studies once a day. Another thing that would've been more rewarding is if I unlocked new furniture and had a reason to decorate. Resources were too scarce and valuable; I had to prioritize building houses and farms. Even if I did decorate, I rarely saw the interiors because the villagers would just stand outside. I would be more willing if they asked for furniture as a gift. There were so many repetitive, pointless tasks; I spent most of my time simply avoiding punishment. I stopped getting gift requests, so eventually the only thing I did was chase villagers down and feed them figs and apples. Even if I completed everything I could, the village's problems just kept spiraling. Checking the front door was pointless if I had enough villagers. I didn't want to waste my time getting cursed or turning down another random stranger. It would've been nice if I didn't have to check the door at every shift, especially after I couldn't bring more villagers in. If an angel came around every so often to give me a gift, then I would finally have a good reason to check the door. I started looking at the demons on purpose just to make the game feel less monotonous. Feeding villagers was pointless unless they went on strike and stopped working during the day shift. They got hungry so fast and food was so limited that it wasn't worth it to try to keep them fed. I hated when villagers begged for food while they were asleep and I couldn't feed them. Overall I just wish there were more ups and downs instead of just downs. Like I said, this game has sooooo much potential. Other bugs or problems I noticed: - Textures would randomly glitch and flash like a strobe light. - If I tried to click on UI elements in a scrolling container, it would just try to scroll without selecting the element. - The particles from the sinners going to church crashed my game twice. - In the beginning, I had no idea how to assign workers to anything, which I wish the angel Gabriel could've told me. - God's judgement would kill a villager and their body didn't exist, yet it would constantly tell me a body was nearby.

The general consensus I've been seeing, and the one I personally subscribe myself to, is that the game scratches that itch of a modern game using Mii like character, and the character creation is very good and easy to understand. However that's where my praise sadly stops. The biggest issue I have is the locked camera, the lack of a ok tutorial, intead bumbling into the mechanics by clicking on random icons/Models in the game world to find menus, as well as a lack of a opening that makes my message and objective clear. I truely felt aimless when I started the game, and honestly had to go online to watch someone else who knew how to play the game show me what I can and can't do. I legitimately had no Idea I had to click on different buildings and structures to assign people to there roles, or even just skip a day by sleeping in a bed. On top of that, having your tutorial, if you can call it that, be a conversation thread and a dialog tree with an npc in the corner of your church is a bit disappointing. In the games current state, and I am aware it is only just entered early access, It has the potential to be a good colony simulater, but In my opinion, having a decent tutorial is always a priority. That feeling of aimlessness did not make me feel confident with playing the game. As of right now, In its current state, I can not recommend this game, but I hope that I can in the future.

This review was rewritten on 07 01 2026. I had a chance to speak with the developer of the game and they confirmed they had removed the previous issue with the star of david. I appreciate that they gave me the opportunity to share my feedback and hold a longer conversation. The dev mentioned that they did not want to be called a fascist or a nazi, and overall i am hopeful that the game will continue to improve in the future. The point of the game is that you are creating "bad people", however i do still feel that in many ways the game fails to specifically punish certain actions. for example, the Nazi Reighsadler Eagle is available as a tattoo for your sinner. Currently, if you give your sinner this tattoo, it does not result in any large punishment for your character. If i was making this game, i would make it so that this nazi eagle tattoo gives your character a special character trait, and changes their stats to make them more dangerous. this would help enforce the core themes of the game without accidentaly glorifying nazi imagery. As it stands, i still don't recommend sinner maker at this point in time, but i am hopeful that may change in the future. i will pay active attention to the game and see how it evolves moving forward. Original review: I was interested in the concept, however there is a lot of Nazi imagery present in the game, such as Nazi Reichsadler Eagle. [strike] Placing a Star of David tattoo on your character increases their "greed" by 10 points, which is antisemetic. [/strike] (has now been fixed) If problematic content like this was removed in a future patch and the developer apolgized, i would consider purchasing the game and continuing to play. However, due to this hateful content i am going to request a refund.

（虽然steam显示我才玩了59分钟，实际上我有大概6小时左右游戏时间是直接打开游戏玩的，所以没显示在steam上） 体验感受： 虽然目前功能还很少，但感觉很有潜力的一部游戏，期待未来增加的新功能/机制 现在村民之间的互动机制除了对话和好感系统外基本没有，应该是还没开始完善？我猜起码有一半人来玩主要是来吃角色互动的，如果这方面做得很丰富绝对会大卖，比如角色互动动画，特殊事件，三角恋四角恋五角恋（？），偷看角色洗澡（？），卡通被窝蠕动象征性做爱（？），村民好几天没出房间结果进屋子发现在上吊（？）之类。这作看上去是非全年龄向，搞点恶俗和血腥的互动感觉会挺有趣的 总之，如果能把互动方面机制写丰富，我宣布这将成为脚踢新版tomodachi life之作，如果难度还能刚刚好维持在勉强活着村子里乱成一锅粥但又不至于崩局的情况那真是无敌了 建议： -希望未来前发和后发部件能分开啊！ -做饭机制有点令人困惑，我家材料齐全，但厨房三个10~20+属性的厨师1天只能做出一个菜，不知道是不是我做错了什么，确实是没看懂。如果解锁了快餐店，再加上每次仪式给50%蜡烛，基本就不需要烧饭这个机制了，可能快餐店或者蜡烛设置有点超模 我遇到的BUG： -放哨的站岗塔安排人工作后，人还是会在楼下闲逛，有时候还会锁在房间里，但状态处于工作中，无法正常对话，把角色从岗位撤下来才会突然瞬移到站岗塔楼下门口 [spoiler] -在日食（吗？）的日子，如果触发变树事件的角色刚好在工作，就没法和他互动（他会说滚啊我在工作），也就没法给他七宗罪小球治愈他，这导致我当时以为这不是需要马上处理的紧急事件，结果跳到下一个时间段角色立马变树了。虽然我估计手动把他撤下工作岗位就可以解决，但这样没啥沉浸感，干脆触发这个事件后角色就别工作了我觉得也行 -角色变成树之后，不同时间段，树里卡着的角色模型可能会变成别的角色（我这边会变成我的主控角色），不知道是有意为之还是BUG[spoiler]

The game has three main points of intrigue: Character creator, management sim, themeing/storytelling. While in early development, you can tell that the tomidochi life style of character creator and the freedom to make custom parts is pretty well done. Its fun and was a big draw for me. Management sims. Character creator has the most polish of the game. Management sim side has bugs and currently drops players in without a tutorial. It has a day cycle and you match sinners with tasks based on their sin stats. Themeing and storytelling from what we see in early access comes out strong with initial vibe. Early 2000's edgy and religious angst, tongue in cheek, I was for it. But ultimately the theming is where the game killed it for me and made me lose faith in seeing the game develop and grow more and just return it. I'm accepting that the 2000's gothic edge either is just set dressing or that there is a theme being deliberately played with. But with the devs response to the star of david being +10 greed that just made me lose all faith in any sort of good writing or satisfying story coming from the game if it is going for actually playing with this being a cruel world with a cruel God and crueler demons. So if the reasoning for +10 greed is "it's an internet joke/meme" as the dev says, then I feel that the themeing is just set dressing. Set dressing alone would be fine but the "OMG!! EDGY!!!!" funni antisemitism is obnoxious. For any actual substance of the game, Im not confident in any satisfying or interesting religious theming from devs that have nothing to say on star of david = +10 greed than "it's a meme".

Sooo good, the gameplay loop is addictive. The character editor is very easy to understand and offers a wide range of options (though I would like a few more curly hair options). The dialogs are fun but I wish they were a little more variated since sometimes they dont fit a sinner's traits. There are a few bugs here and there but theyre not super annoying and theyre easy to get past. The only annoying bug ive encountered is that when you ask someone who is inside a house to talk w someone outside a house or vice versa they wont talk but the game will continue telling u that theres a convo going on until u quit the game and start again but honestly is more of a visual annoyance than an actual problem while playing. Also I wish that the church stopped telling u that theres nothing being studied once u finish it. I hope that list becomes an useful stat in the future too (my lustful sinners are useless.... theyre all unemployed all the time). Other than those things everything else is amazing and I've had sooo much fun with this game!

The game is really fun! I'm still upgrading certain things and making sure my village is expanding. The dialogue exchanges are funny, and the character creator is fun to experiment with. I also like the part where your own custom made sinners come knocking at the door with unique dialogue, that was a nice touch. I like the church where you can upgrade your stats and unlock options, it gives me a goal to go toward. Some parts of the game are confusing though, such as the restaurant option where sinners feed themselves. For me at least, despite having up the restaurant or fast food option, they won't go and feed themselves or buy their own food. I'm not sure if I'm doing something wrong or if it's just a bug on my end, but having to go up to them to feed them constantly gets a little tiring. Additionally, I wish that the romance options between characters were more common, especially characters who are flirty or have the lover card. None of my sinners really do anything other than ask for gifts or food, I feel like they don't interact with each other much other than occasional dialogue exchanges. I just would like it if they asked chief to make friends with each other much more often, or to hang out with each other, things of that nature. My favorite part of the game is the unique concept of it! The whole rapture, apocalyptic setting is very interesting to me, and it's fun to play to get your upgrades and make more sinners. The game is very well done for early release, and I look forward to seeing more updates!

There are varying positives and negatives to this game. The customisation is fun and an upgrade to Tomodachi life, you can custom-make your own parts, the options for clothing items/accesories are limited however I understand its early access and will look forward to what they add in the future. The tarot cards (which also shows the mbti alignment) are a nice way to show their personality along with the seven deadly sins. The dialogue for the characters are funny but limited, have minor grammatical errors and are a little absurd. There are unfortunately a lot of bugs like the trade post not existing, characters stuck in houses, randomly dissapearing, when a character is stuck in a certain place they are unable to converse with another character and a whole lot more. Basically throughout the whole gameplay I was searching up how to do things due to Gabriel, the very unhelpful messenger didn't provide me any help at all other than give answers to questions that were common sense. Because of this I found the gameplay to be quite boring and repetitive as I was watching the days going by watching my sinners die and being confused on what to do. I will leave a good rating for now as it has a lot of potential and I hope they don't ruin it.

A very promising vertical slice that is also very tasteful about its Y2K subject matter. Its probably the best "playable creepypasta" type thing. It actually has modding support and already alot of custom character parts made by the community. Its genuinely made with love and is an insane balancing act between horror and comedy. The game itself is very buggy and there isn't much in terms of actual gameplay. But, so far, I have trust that this project will become something great. Updates are pretty frequent so far. It also shows a genuine respect for religion not found most media. Its much smarter than something like Trench Crusade or most media that relies on shock/smugness to carry its narrative. If you know much about religion, history, or the bible you will find that the game is pretty studious on the subject -- in a very real way that exonerates it.

As other reviews stated, insane amount of fascist imagery in this game, which I unfortunately didn't notice until having spent multiple hours in the game because the UI is so bad I didn't notice half of the character creation menu at first. Other than that, the game's systems are closed off and uninteresting. the relationships don't seem to have any consequences on any other gameplay mechanics, there's a research tree that doesn't need to exist at all, the game is buggy and doesn't really seem to have any thought put into it. While I understand that this is an early access game, the foundation is shaky and I really can't see this ever becoming a good game.

There is just alot of game-hindering/breaking bugs in general at the time I wrote this, and there isn't really enough interesting interaction/content to justify myself playing the main village mode much further.

This game is actually a lot more fun than I expected. Even if buggy (which should isn't surprising, this is early access after all) Character creator has a lot of liberty, gameplay loop is addictive, artstyle is cool. I think my issue with this stems from the fact that while this game is satire, it kind of loops around to just perpetuating stereotypes and from what Im seeing, it is attracting people who support and believe in said stereotypes. From what I read this wasn't the creators intention and they have actually changed bits of the game because of the reviews. Props to them, more game developers need to start doing that. Anyway I understand you're making sinners, I just dont think the game is exactly "punishing" said sinners. Im taking this from a review by Sherf where they mentioned that the Nazi Reighsadler Eagle tattoo doesnt contribute to any big punishments. Its okay to include dark themes in the game, its just important to potray them for what they are. Otherwise it will most likely come off as tone deaf to most, or even worse they will think that the creator actually is a nazi (which I believe isnt the case, but I did see that some people think that). The other group of people that think this makes the game cool either have the reddit basement dweller badge or are edgy 12 year olds. Anyway, I will be refunding this game.
